name: Finite Channels, Fisher Information and Cramér-Rao Bounds
description: Builds finite stochastic channels, distributions and parametric families, proves Fisher data processing under a fixed Markov kernel and the finite Cramér-Rao bound for locally unbiased estimators, and gives the sharp quadratic lower bound on binary entropy.

program.name: Statistical and Analytic Instances
program.summary: The statistics results build finite stochastic channels and parametric families, prove Fisher data processing under a fixed Markov kernel and the finite Cramér-Rao bound, and give the sharp quadratic bound on binary entropy. The analytic results give positivity of integer binary quadratic forms, uniform inversion under compact separation and Hermitian kernel realizations.

oneLine: Finite Fisher information contracts under fixed Markov kernels and lower-bounds unbiased estimator variance, while binary entropy admits a sharp quadratic lower bound.
summary: Finite distributions, stochastic channels, regular parametric families with zero-sum tangents, scores, Fisher information, locally unbiased estimators and binary entropy are the objects. The questions are how Fisher information behaves under a fixed Markov kernel, when processing preserves Fisher, what variance floor unbiased estimation obeys, and what quadratic floor binary entropy obeys. Under probability and tangent pushforward hypotheses Fisher contracts with loss equal to the mean squared score residual, equality holds in the characterized score-preserved cases, locally unbiased estimators with positive Fisher satisfy variance at least one over Fisher, and binary entropy on [0, 1] lies above four log two times p times one minus p. The half-Bernoulli family attains the variance floor with Fisher four and variance one quarter, the entropy bound is recorded tight at one half, and finite-sample gate floors follow from the same Cauchy-Schwarz pattern under stated moment and integrability hypotheses. Interior parameters, positive support, positive Fisher and the pushforward identities are required throughout. Probability transfer without the tangent identity does not enforce contraction, and zero-Fisher constant models lie outside the positive-Fisher division.
boundary: On the informative side a fixed kernel carrying both probability and tangent pushforwards never raises Fisher information and the drop equals the mean squared score residual, with equality holding if and only if input scores are preserved on every possible output. On the other side probability transfer alone can raise Fisher, zero-Fisher constant families admit no positive-Fisher division for the variance floor, and constant-one tangents and mass above one are impossible. The contraction theorem, its score-preservation equivalences, the variance bound with its outside cases, and the sharp entropy lower bound with recorded tightness at one half locate the boundary.

conclusions.statement: For finite types Omega and Gamma, families F and G and channel K, if every output probability is the kernel pushforward of input probabilities and every output tangent is the kernel pushforward of input tangents, then Fisher information of G is at most Fisher information of F.

For finite types Omega and Gamma, families F and G and channel K, under the same probability and tangent pushforward hypotheses, Fisher information of F minus Fisher information of G equals the double sum over outputs and inputs of input probability times kernel mass times squared score residual.
For a finite index type and family F, any locally unbiased estimator E with positive Fisher information satisfies one over Fisher information is at most estimator variance of its estimate.
For every real p with 0 <= p and p <= 1, 4 * Real.log 2 * (p * (1 - p)) is at most Real.binEntropy p.

Under the same probability and tangent pushforward hypotheses, Fisher information of G equals Fisher information of F if and only if for all inputs and outputs with strictly positive kernel mass, the input score equals the output score.

Under the same probability and tangent pushforward hypotheses, Fisher information of G equals Fisher information of F if and only if any two inputs that can both reach the same output with positive mass have equal input scores.

On a Fintype Omega, if 0 < N, 0 < FI, the sum of centered estimator times score equals 1, variance equals the sum of squared centered estimator, and N * FI equals the sum of squared score, then 1 / (N * FI) is at most variance.

On a Fintype Omega, if 0 < N, the sum of centered estimator times score equals 1, variance equals the sum of squared centered estimator, and N * binaryFisherInformation 0 equals the sum of squared score, then 1 / (4 * N) is at most variance.

If epsilon is nonzero, the sum of centered estimator times score over Fin 2 equals 1, variance equals the sum of squared centered estimator, and epsilonGateSampleCount epsilon times binaryFisherInformation 0 equals the sum of squared score, then epsilon^2 / (2 * Real.log 2) is at most variance.

If 0 < sigma, p is pointwise positive, the integral of p equals 1, the integral of p times (x - mu)^2 equals sigma^2, and p, p times (x - mu)^2, p times log p, p times log g and g times (x - mu)^2 are integrable where g is the Gaussian witness, then differential entropy of p is at most differential entropy of g.
For the half-Bernoulli family and half estimator, Fisher information equals 4, estimator variance equals 1 / 4, and variance equals one over Fisher information.
The identity channel sends constant binary probabilities to Bernoulli-half probabilities and yet Fisher information of Bernoulli-half is not at most Fisher information of the constant family.
It is not the case that Fisher information of the constant binary family is positive.

For families F and G and a deterministic map q with DecidableEq on outputs, under pushforward hypotheses through the deterministic channel, Fisher information of G equals Fisher information of F if and only if inputs with equal q values have equal scores.

openPoints: Fisher contraction needs a fixed kernel with both probability and tangent pushforward identities; pushforward and curve constructions carry positivity, differentiability and local normalization hypotheses.

Cramer-Rao needs strictly positive Fisher information; the constant binary family lies outside, the Bernoulli instance needs a strictly interior parameter, and the constant-zero estimator has zero derivative and lies outside unbiasedness.
Parametric families need positive support and zero-sum tangent; channel rows and distribution masses need finiteness with mass at most one.

Binary entropy bound needs p in [0, 1]; Gaussian maximum entropy needs pointwise positivity, normalization, second-moment and integrability hypotheses; finite-sample bounds need positive N and Fisher with cross-sum one and matching variance and score-sum identities; the epsilon gate needs nonzero epsilon.

The certificate contraction field and transport-gap structures are recorded labels proving nothing by themselves; the certificate-based processing statement holds by returning that field and the unbiased derivative identity holds by definition of the estimator structure.

files.summary: The file defines the gap function F p = binEntropy p minus 4*log 2*p*(1-p) and proves auxiliary derivative and monotonicity facts for it. It proves the log-ratio bound, nonpositivity of the gap derivative on (2/9, 1/2), the left-piece inequality on (0, 2/9], and nonnegativity of F on [0, 1/2]. From these plus binEntropy symmetry it proves the sharp quadratic bound 4*log 2*p*(1-p) <= binEntropy p for p in [0, 1], a bound noted as absent from Mathlib. It also proves equality at p = 1/2 where both sides equal log 2.
files.conclusion: For every real p in [0, 1], 4*log 2*p*(1-p) is at most binEntropy p, with equality at p = 1/2.

files.summary: This file defines a finite stochastic channel as a family of normalized finite distributions, one output law for each input outcome. It constructs deterministic channels from ordinary functions via point-mass distributions, with the identity channel as a special case. It proves that every channel row assigns mass at most one to each output. It therefore proves that no row assigns mass above one.
files.conclusion: No row of a finite stochastic channel ever assigns mass greater than one.

files.summary: This file defines canonical normalized finite distributions, deterministic point masses, adapters to and from the legacy observer-kernel distribution, and the fair binary law. It proves every mass is at most one, the point-mass and binary values, and that no normalized law assigns mass above one.
files.conclusion: Every normalized finite law has mass at most one, with point masses and the fair binary law as examples.

files.summary: This file defines a Bernoulli family and estimator at interior parameters and their half-parameter fixtures. It computes Fisher information four and variance one quarter with exact Cramer-Rao equality. It shows the biased constant-zero estimator has derivative zero, outside the theorem.
files.conclusion: The half-Bernoulli family has Fisher information four and variance one quarter, attaining Cramer-Rao, while the constant-zero estimator lies outside.

files.summary: This file defines estimator variance and proves a weighted Cauchy-Schwarz lemma and the native finite Cramer-Rao bound for locally unbiased estimators with positive Fisher information. It shows the constant binary family has non-positive Fisher and lies outside.
files.conclusion: Every locally unbiased estimator with positive Fisher information satisfies variance at least one over Fisher information.

files.summary: Defines finite parametric families, Fisher information, finite Markov kernels, and a FisherMarkovCertificate recording pushforward identities for probability and tangent plus a contraction field. Proves Fisher information contracts under a fixed kernel with the loss equal to the mean squared score residual, and characterizes equality as preservation of scores on every possible output or fiber. Provides pushforward, curve, and certificate constructions, and shows probability transfer alone does not imply contraction via a Bernoulli versus constant binary counterexample.
files.conclusion: Fisher information contracts under a fixed finite Markov kernel with loss equal to the mean squared score residual, equality holds exactly when scores are preserved on every possible output, and probability transfer alone does not imply contraction.

files.summary: This file defines Fisher information as probability-weighted squared score. It proves nonnegativity, zero for the constant binary family, and that positive Fisher cannot be zero. Only regular local families are treated.
files.conclusion: Fisher information is nonnegative, zero for the constant family, and positive Fisher is nonzero.

files.summary: This file defines regular finite parametric families by a normalized positive law and zero-sum tangent. It builds a parameter-insensitive fair binary family with zero tangent. It proves the zero tangent and impossibility of constant-one tangents.
files.conclusion: Regular finite families need zero-sum tangents and positive support, so no family has constant-one tangent.

files.summary: This file defines the score as tangent over strictly positive probability. It proves probability times score recovers the tangent, hence the probability-weighted score has mean zero, with all constant-family scores zero. Only regular finite support is treated.
files.conclusion: Scores have zero mean because probability times score recovers the tangent.

files.summary: This file defines expectation, tangent derivative expectation, locally unbiased estimators and score covariance. It proves covariance equals derivative expectation, hence unbiased estimators have derivative one and score covariance one. Only local unbiasedness at the parameter is treated.
files.conclusion: Score covariance equals derivative expectation, so locally unbiased estimators have unit score covariance.

files.summary: The file defines differential entropy, weighted expectation and variance on finite sample spaces, binary Fisher information, the epsilon-N sample-count gate, and a Gaussian witness density. It proves a Gaussian maximum-entropy theorem under fixed normalization and centered second moment, with KL-gap entropy bounds and a measure-uniqueness equality case. It proves a finite-sample Cramér–Rao variance lower bound from Cauchy–Schwarz, its binary specialization at Fisher information four, an explicit two-point saturating instance, and a gate-rewritten variance floor.
files.conclusion: Under fixed normalization and second moment the Gaussian density maximizes differential entropy, and any finite unbiased score model obeys variance at least one over N times Fisher information with an explicit binary gate saturation.
